title: 'Best Targets Tonight' transit times are computed for the night after tomorrow - every time is ~8 minutes wrong
closed_by: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/mosaic_targets.dart:138 (ref.watch(_currentNightDateProvider)), the provider it reads at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/catalog_astronomy.dart:153-157, and the helper packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:1240-1247 (AstronomyCalculations.nightDateOf)
summary: A later wave replaced the dusk-timestamp anchor with a night-date anchor. bestTargetsProvider no longer computes twilight and passes astronomicalDusk as `date`; it watches _currentNightDateProvider, which is AstronomyCalculations.nightDateOf(observationTime) - local noon to local noon, so an instant past midnight names the day the night STARTED. calculateObjectVisibility still builds its window as DateTime(date.year,.month,.day,12)+24h (astronomy_calculations.dart:1286-1287), which is now correct because the caller hands it a night date. The Info-tab half is closed by the same provider at equipment_view.dart:150. I checked every production caller of calculateObjectVisibility: target_scoring.dart:233/420, planning_overlays.dart:44, content_sections.dart:467/860, target_preview_tooltip.dart:60, target_queue_panel.dart:173, full_timeline.dart:115, plan_tonight_sequencer_helper.dart:207, sequence_time_estimator.dart:776 and altitude_chart.dart:236 all route through nightDateOf; none still passes a raw instant.
test: packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/tonight_night_window_test.dart - 5 tests, all pass. 'Best Targets and the Info tab agree on which night they describe' drives the real bestTargetsProvider and selectedObjectVisibilityProvider through a ProviderContainer at 02:00 local, 40N/105W.
revert_check: Reverted mosaic_targets.dart:138 from `ref.watch(_currentNightDateProvider)` to `ref.watch(_currentDateProvider)` (severs the production wiring, not the helper). Test failed: Expected DateTime:<2026-08-03 00:52:48> Actual DateTime:<2026-08-04 00:48:52> - the exact 00:52-vs-00:48 contradiction the finding reported. Restored; 5/5 pass.
caveats: The verifier's own correction stands: the slip is ONE night / ~4 minutes, not two sidereal days.

title: Residual found while closing the depth finding: a deep-star manifest with no declared floor re-opened the mag 9-11.5 hole
summary: DeepStarManifest.fromJson defaulted magnitudeFloor to 11.5 - the last live instance of the retired constant, and the one place it still had teeth. deep_star_providers.dart:99 hands the store `minMagnitude: math.max(kHygFaintFloorMag, manifest.magnitudeFloor)`, so a manifest omitting the field made the tier discard every star between mag 9 and 11.5 - precisely the magnitudes the bundled HYG catalog does not hold either, leaving a hole where the tier exists to fill one. That is the same empty-imaging-FOV symptom the parent finding is about, surviving in the seam after the copy was fixed. Defaulting to kHygFaintFloorMag is strictly safe: the seam can only over-request (asking below a tileset's real cutoff returns what it has), never under-request.
test: packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/deep_star_hyg_seam_test.dart :: 'a manifest with no declared floor does not re-open the mag 9-11.5 hole' - parses a real manifest JSON with the field omitted, then drives deepStarsInViewProvider at 1.2 deg FOV and asserts both the seam value and that the 9.5/10.4/11.2 stars survive.
revert_check: Reverted deep_star_tile.dart:432 to `magnitudeFloor: (json['magnitudeFloor'] as num?)?.toDouble() ?? 11.5;` (and dropped the hyg_depth.dart import). Test failed: Expected <9.0> Actual <11.5>. Restored; 4/4 pass.
caveats: Latent rather than live today - tools/catalog_prep always writes magnitudeFloor, so only a hand-written manifest hit the fallback. No public tileset exists yet.
